summary: QUORUM all up: speculating executor, one data read (10.0.0.3, ring order) plus a local digest, digests computed from data match, no repair. Path matches AbstractReadExecutor/ReadCallback/DigestResolver.

Live-cell divergence reproduced end to end (data-driven mismatch, full data reads, newest wins, blocking READ_REPAIR_REQ rewrites the stale memtable). But replicas strip tombstones before responding, so a newer deletion loses and deleted data is resurrected and 'repaired' onto the tombstone holder (code merges unfiltered data, DataResolver.java:315-317). Repair writes are silently dropped as unknown table unless keyspace.tables seeds shop.users (contract seam with write-path). Repair mutation is the full partition, not the per-replica diff.
Via CQL: two replicas down gives unavailable 0x1000 {alive 1, required 2} from ReplicaPlans.assureSufficientLiveReplicas before any message.

Hung chosen replica at ONE: model speculates a data read to the next candidate and returns its rows, but only after the 5000ms timeout (code: at 2500ms sample latency). A slow-but-answering replica (3000ms) never triggers speculation. Needs concurrent in-flight calls / wait-until-T-or-k-of-n.

Corrected: with 99p and all 3 up, one silent replica is speculated around and the read succeeds. Timeout needs no spare replica (e.g. one down + one silent): NeverSpeculating executor, ReadTimeout 0x1200 at 5000ms with received 1 < blockFor 2, data_present false. Model reproduces both, via coordinator-read and CQL.

Failure threshold reproduced: replicas fail with READ_TOO_MANY_TOMBSTONES, coordinator signals immediately, client gets read-failure 0x1300, no speculation. Warning: logged and counted per replica, but ClientWarn.warn (ReadCommand.java:631) on the coordinator's local read is not modeled, so the client never sees the warning.

Memtable+sstable merge, newest cell wins, cell tombstone and partition deletion shadowing (ts <= markedForDeleteAt) and bloom skip reproduced. Path incomplete: all sstables are one aggregate row per partition (no per-sstable bloom/max-timestamp ordering/early stop, no timestamp-order names path). Equal-timestamp tie keeps the memtable value instead of Cells.reconcile's greater value.
